name: vertex-cpm-fluctuation-match
title: Vertex → CPM fluctuation match
question: Can the vertex (tyssue) backend reproduce the CPM's emergent interaction pattern on the large Sego 2022 blueprint — its per-cell motility, boundary fluctuation and neighbour-exchange statistics — WITHOUT folding the mesh? Today the honest CPM-matching motility/noise values invert short junctions and self-intersect the polygons, so they were capped, leaving the vertex epithelium ~5x less mobile and far more ordered than the CPM. This study asks whether a mesh-safe mechanism closes that gap under a quantitative distance-to-CPM target.

purpose.question: Is the vertex/CPM pattern gap a tuning problem (bounded by capped knobs) or a mechanism problem (vertex lacks a CPM-faithful, T1-safe fluctuation source)?
purpose.mechanism: CPM advances a stochastically-roughened voxel interface by Metropolis boundary flips at temperature; the vertex fork advances a confluent, gap-free polygon tiling by grad-E displacement plus discrete T1/T2/T3 neighbour swaps. The CPM's per-voxel fluctuation has no direct vertex analog — it is approximated by OU junction-tension noise plus an active-Brownian random walk, both of which fold the mesh at CPM-matching amplitude and were therefore capped (adhesion-calibration).
purpose.expected_outcome: Either (A) a mesh-safe fluctuation mechanism drives the vertex motility/roughness metrics into a tolerance band around the CPM while mesh validity holds over the full run, or (B) it does not, and we report the residual honestly as a structural limit of the vertex substrate (an HONEST OPEN QUESTION), not a forced pass.

key_assumptions: The CPM is the reference substrate; vertex is judged by distance-to-CPM on the shared large Sego 2022 blueprint, same seeds.
Mesh validity (no inverted/self-intersecting faces over the whole run) is a HARD constraint — a metric match bought by a folded mesh does not count.
Only mechanisms/parameters already in the vertex backend (or a new T1-safe fluctuation term proposed here) are used; no literature value is folded in to force a target (see falsifiability).

The quantitative target depends on the new cross-paradigm behavior metrics (per-cell displacement/MSD distance, neighbour-graph distance over time, infection-front-speed distance) shipped alongside this investigation.

readouts.name: epithelial_msd
readouts.description: Mean-squared displacement of the epithelial (H) cohort over the run; the headline motility gap (CPM ~9.5 vs vertex ~2.2 um^2 today).

readouts.name: immune_displacement_median
readouts.description: Median net displacement of immune cells over the run (CPM ~9.4 vs vertex ~4.6 um today).

readouts.name: area_cv
readouts.description: Coefficient of variation of cell area over the run — boundary-fluctuation proxy (CPM ~0.093 vs vertex ~0.038 today).

readouts.name: infection_front_speed
readouts.description: Advance rate of the I-patch front (spatial_pattern front vs time), per backend.

readouts.name: neighbour_graph_churn
readouts.description: Per-step change in the cell contact graph (neighbour-exchange / graph-distance over time), per backend.

behavior_tests.name: epithelial-motility-matches-cpm
behavior_tests.description: Vertex epithelial MSD lands within a tolerance band of the CPM MSD (not the capped ~5x-low value).

behavior_tests.name: boundary-fluctuation-matches-cpm
behavior_tests.description: Vertex area CV approaches the CPM area CV (today 0.038 vs 0.093).

behavior_tests.name: interaction-pattern-distance-drops
behavior_tests.description: The neighbour-graph-churn and infection-front-speed distances from the CPM drop versus the shipped vertex baseline.

behavior_tests.name: mesh-stays-valid
behavior_tests.description: No inverted or self-intersecting faces at any step of the run (HARD constraint — overrides any metric match).

controls.name: cpm-self-null
controls.description: CPM-vs-CPM (seed-varied) distance is the matched null floor each vertex distance is judged against — a vertex match must approach this floor, not 0.

controls.name: vertex-shipped-baseline
controls.description: The current capped vertex backend — the starting distance-to-CPM every candidate must improve on.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: The gap is pure tuning — raising the capped knobs (sheet_motility, tension_noise) closes it.
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: Tested directly by the vertex-knob-push variant under the mesh-validity gate; if it folds the mesh before matching, tuning alone is refuted.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: The gap is a metric artifact (rasterization / cohort matching), not a real mobility difference.
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: The new metrics operate on continuous positions/neighbour graphs (not only rasters); CPM-self null calibrates the metric's own noise floor.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Vertex confluence (no medium, margin-attached immune) is the dominant cause, not fluctuation amplitude.
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: Separable by the immune-representation arm (free-wandering vs margin-attached) in implementation_requirements.

implementation_requirements.title: Cross-paradigm behavior metrics in compare/metrics.py (displacement/MSD distance, neighbour-graph distance, front-speed distance)
implementation_requirements.description: The minimization target. Ships as reusable infra via a feature PR to main; this study consumes it.

implementation_requirements.title: Per-step mesh-validity invariant exposed from the vertex backend
A T1-safe (sub-threshold) fluctuation term for the vertex backend
implementation_requirements.description: Candidate mesh-safe analog of the CPM temperature: bounded per-vertex jitter / boundary-roughness that cannot shrink a junction past the T1 threshold.
implementation_requirements.defer_until: req-behavior-metrics lands so the effect is measurable.

implementation_requirements.title: Free-wandering vs margin-attached immune representation toggle

design_pivot_required.question: Close the gap by pushing capped knobs, or by adding a new T1-safe fluctuation mechanism?
alternatives: A. Knob-push only — raise sheet_motility / tension_noise under a mesh-validity gate; simplest, may fold before matching.
B. New mesh-safe fluctuation term — bounded per-vertex jitter / boundary roughness; more work, likely required if A folds.
C. Accept the residual — report the capped vertex as an honest structural limit if neither A nor B reaches the band.
design_pivot_required.requested_response: Expert steer on how far to push mechanism changes into the tyssue backend vs accepting an honest residual.

falsifiability: The claim 'vertex can match the CPM interaction pattern on the large Sego model' is overturned if, with mesh validity enforced, no provided mechanism drives the primary distance metrics into their tolerance bands — in which case the honest result is that the vertex substrate cannot reproduce CPM-level fluctuation without folding, and that is reported as the finding rather than patched with an un-provided term to force a pass.
limitations: Planned (Design phase) — no runs yet; all target numbers are the CPM references to approach, not results.
Depends on the new cross-paradigm behavior metrics (req-behavior-metrics) landing first; until then the distances are not computable.
A match on these metrics is necessary but not sufficient for full pattern identity; visual (flipbook) agreement is a secondary check.

report.title: Can vertex reproduce CPM's interaction pattern without folding the mesh?
report.objective: Drive the vertex (tyssue) motility / boundary-fluctuation / interaction-pattern metrics into a tolerance band around the CPM on the large Sego 2022 blueprint, under a hard mesh-validity constraint — or report the residual as a structural limit.
report.caveat: The honest CPM-matching motility folds the vertex mesh today; this study exists to find a mesh-safe mechanism or to document that none of the provided ones suffice.

study_card.goal: Get the vertex backend to reproduce the CPM's emergent interaction pattern on the large Sego model, measured as distance-to-CPM, without folding the mesh.
study_card.mechanism: Replace/augment the capped OU-noise + active-Brownian motility (which folds the mesh at CPM amplitude) with a T1-safe fluctuation source, and judge the result on the new cross-paradigm motility / neighbour-graph / front-speed distances.
study_card.why_before_next: The capstone comparison and any 'all three substrates agree' claim depend on vertex actually reproducing the CPM pattern; this study is where that is won or honestly bounded.
study_card.expected_result: Vertex motility MSD within ~30% of CPM (vs ~5x low today) with a valid mesh, or a documented structural residual.
study_card.main_expert_question: How hard should we push mechanism changes into the tyssue backend before accepting an honest residual (pivot VCF-01)?
